title: Visualize without leaving the present
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you see when you picture the thing you want?
I asked: you are thirsty and you want a glass of water; you open the refrigerator, what do you see? I used it to show how a picture appears when you need something.
I said that an athlete who has spent a year building toward a race and stands on the blocks waiting for the gun is living the visualization they have built.

I said that there is a word people use, manifestation, which I do not like to use: you predict something will happen and it does. To me it is mental discipline dedicated to doing something over and over.
I said to be careful if you are constantly visualizing, because you can visualize and not be in the present.

groups.heading: Take it to the here and now

lines.text: A student said that you may have a deep visualization of the destination and of the path to it, but then you have to take it to the here and now and execute on that path.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you picture for next year.
Write the picture of the path.
Write today's step on that path.
Write how long you will picture it each day.
Write what you will do so that you stay present.

check.q: What did I say manifestation really is?
choices: Mental discipline done over and over

check.q: What did I warn about visualizing?
choices: You can be absent from the present

check.q: What did a student say you must do with the path?
choices: Execute it in the here and now

recap: Picture it. Practise it. Act in the present.
